title: Grinshpun–Sárközy conjecture on tiling bounded-degree graph sequences
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{F}={F_1,F_2,\dots\}$ be a graph sequence with $v(F_i)=i$ and maximum degree $\Delta(F_i)\leq\Delta$ for all $i$. For an $r$-edge coloured complete graph, let $\tau_r(\mathcal{F})$ be the least $s$ such that its vertex set has a monochromatic $\mathcal{F}$-tiling of size at most $s$, where a monochromatic $\mathcal{F}$-tiling consists of monochromatic subgraphs, each isomorphic to an element of $\mathcal{F}$, whose vertex sets partition the complete graph's vertex set.

**Grinshpun–Sárközy conjecture.** For every positive integer $r$ there exists a constant $C_r$ such that, for every $\Delta\geq 2$ and every $\Delta$-bounded graph sequence $\mathcal{F}$,

$$
tau_r(\mathcal{F})\leq \exp(\Delta^{C_r}).
$$

The conjecture concerns the finiteness and quantitative growth of the tiling number for more than two colours. Corsten and Mendonça later proved finiteness with a triple-exponential bound, and the paper proves the stronger bound $\tau_r(\mathcal{F})\leq\exp(C_r\Delta)$ for bipartite bounded-degree graph sequences, but the full conjecture for general sequences is not resolved here.
quantifiers_reviewed: For every r exists C_r, for every Delta>=2 and every Delta-bounded sequence, uniformly over complete-graph orders and r-colorings.
technical_assessment: A bipartite embedding bound does not handle arbitrary bounded-degree pieces; a finite coloring test cannot establish uniform tiling-number growth. No short absorption/embedding mechanism is supplied.

title: The NFM separated-eigenvector conjecture under Dirichlet noise
statement_exact_utf8:

$$
V_j':= \{i\in[n]:\theta^i_j\geq t(k,\bm{\alpha})\},\qquad
\Theta_j:=\Theta(V_j',:).

$$
4.4\Theta_j\Theta_j^T-2.2E

is well separated from the remaining eigenvalues and its corresponding eigenvector is positive.

title: Sparse average-case k-SUM conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
In the $(k,N,r)$-SUM problem, the input consists of $r$ elements $z_1,\ldots,z_r$, independently and uniformly chosen from $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$. The goal is to find an ordered $k$-tuple of distinct indices $K=\{i_1,\ldots,i_k\}$ such that

$$
\sum_{j\in K}z_j=0,
$$

where the sum is over $\mathbb{Z}$. The sparse regime has only a few solutions on average, with $r^k\approx N$. **Sparse average-case $k$-SUM conjecture.** Any algorithm that solves the $(k,N,r)$-SUM problem with $r=N^{1/k}$ and probability $\Omega_k(1)$ has expected running time at least

$$
T=\Omega_k\left(r^{\lceil k/2\rceil-o(1)}\right).
$$

The conjecture is presented as folklore hardness of the uniform distribution under a standard computational model and underlies the paper's conditional optimality results for dense $k$-SUM.
quantifiers_reviewed: For each fixed k every success-Omega_k(1) algorithm at r=N^(1/k) has expected time Omega_k(r^(ceil(k/2)-o(1))).
technical_assessment: Computational model, input bit cost and preprocessing rules are not specified. This is a distributional lower bound, not a small deterministic zero-sum certificate.

title: Kawasaki dynamics mixing conjecture for the fixed-magnetization Ising model
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$, and consider the fixed-magnetization Ising model with inverse temperature $\beta$ and magnetization parameter $\eta$. The Kawasaki dynamics has two versions: local flip dynamics, proposing swaps of spins across an edge, and global flip dynamics, proposing swaps of arbitrary spins. Let $\beta_c(\Delta)$ and $\eta_c(\Delta,\beta)$ denote the threshold parameters in the paper.

**Kawasaki dynamics mixing conjecture.** For $\beta<\beta_c(\Delta)$, the Kawasaki dynamics mix in time polynomial in $n$ for any fixed magnetization and any graph $G$ of maximum degree $\Delta$. For $\beta>\beta_c(\Delta)$ and $|\eta|>\eta_c(\Delta,\beta)$, they mix in time polynomial in $n$ for any fixed magnetization $k\geq\eta n$ and any such graph. In both cases, the global flip dynamics mix in time $O(n\log n)$.

This conjecture concerns the efficiency of a standard local Markov-chain sampler for the fixed-magnetization Ising model, complementing the paper’s approximation results. The source does not provide evidence of a resolution, so the conjecture remains open; the relation between the one-sentence rapid-mixing claim and the more detailed parameterized formulation should be checked.
quantifiers_reviewed: All bounded-degree graphs, two temperature/magnetization regimes, polynomial local mixing and O(n log n) global mixing.
technical_assessment: Threshold definitions and magnetization convention are omitted; disconnected graphs make local irreducibility material. Such a domain issue earns no outcome, and does not resolve the global sampler claim.

title: Uniform minimization conjecture for light-traffic coefficients
statement_exact_utf8:
Consider a redundancy system with $N$ servers and edge-selection probabilities $P=(p_{\{i,j\}})_{i,j}$, where $i,j\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$ and $i\ne j$. For each $q\geq 0$, let $\alpha_q(P)$ denote the coefficient governing the light-traffic probability of having at least $q$ jobs. Let $P'=(p'_{\{i,j\}})_{i,j}$ be the uniform policy, with

$$
p'_{\{i,j\}}=\frac{1}{\binom{N}{2}}.
$$

**Uniform minimization conjecture.** For every $q\geq 0$, the coefficient under the uniform policy equals the minimum over all edge-selection probability vectors:

$$
\alpha_q^*\coloneqq\alpha_q(P')=\min\left\{\alpha_q(P)\mid P=(p_{\{i,j\}})_{i,j}\right\}.
$$

This optimization conjecture would imply the uniform sampling dominance conjecture in the light-traffic regime through the stated comparison of tail probabilities. The coefficients are continuous functions on the compact set of edge-selection probabilities, so a minimum exists; what remains open is proving that the uniform policy attains it for every $q$.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every q>=0 and N, all edge probability vectors: alpha_q(P_uniform) attains the minimum.
technical_assessment: Coefficient alpha_q is not given as a formula. Symmetry plus continuity proves neither convexity nor global minimization. A small polynomial/Hessian route needs the exact redundancy-model coefficients.

title: The bosonic and fermionic polynomial degree conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $k$ indistinguishable bosons have $G={\rm SU}(N)$ with $N={{n+k-1}\choose{k}}$, and let $k$ indistinguishable fermions have $G={\rm SU}(K)$ with $K={{n}\choose{k}}$. In both cases, let $H\cong {\rm SU}(n)$ and

$$
\mathfrak{t}\cong\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n\ \middle|\ \sum_{j=1}^n x_j=0\right\}.

\Delta_{\mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{h}}(x)=P_{\mathrm{bos}}(x_1,\ldots,x_n),\qquad \Delta_{\mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{h}}(x)=P_{\mathrm{fer}}(x_1,\ldots,x_n),

where these are homogeneous polynomials on the restriction to $\mathfrak{t}$ of the standard coordinates. **The bosonic and fermionic polynomial degree conjecture.** In the setting of the bosonic density formula (respectively, the fermionic density formula), the minimum degree $\ell+2$ of $\Delta_{\mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{h}}$ restricted to any affine line in $\mathfrak{t}$ on which it does not uniformly vanish is equal to the degree of $P_{\mathrm{bos}}$ (respectively, $P_{\mathrm{fer}}$) in any one of the individual variables $x_1,\ldots,x_n$. technical_assessment: The product Delta_g/h, allowed n,k and density parameters are not specified. Generic-line degree equals total degree, not necessarily minimum line degree; a monomial inspection cannot settle the missing restricted product.

title: Popular-difference density conjecture for three-point matrix patterns in the integer lattice
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be $2\times2$ matrices with integer entries such that $M_2-M_1$ has full rank. For any $\alpha,\varepsilon>0$, there exists $N_0=N_0(\alpha,\varepsilon)\in\mathbb N$ such that, whenever $N\ge N_0$ and $A\subseteq\\{1,\dots,N\\}^2$ satisfies $|A|\ge\alpha N^2$, there is a vector $\vec n\in\mathbb Z^2$ with $M_1\vec n,M_2\vec n\ne0$ for which

$$
\left|\left\\{\vec x\in\mathbb Z^2:\{\vec x,\vec x+M_1\vec n,\vec x+M_2\vec n\\}\subseteq A\right\\}\right|>(\alpha^3-\varepsilon)N^2.
$$

**Popular-difference density conjecture.** The displayed lower bound holds for every pair of matrices satisfying the stated full-rank condition. title: The bounded-exception conjecture for Markoff surface orbits

$$

$$

title: Uniform stable approximation conjecture for the parametric approximation sets
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{A}_{P}$ be the finite-dimensional truncation of the parametric Hilbert space $\mathcal{A}$, let $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{P,M}$ denote the first $M$ sampling functionals in the approximation set $\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{P}$, and let $\mathcal{T}_{\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{P,M}}$ be their approximation operator. $$

title: Refined list Hadwiger's conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\lambda$ be a multiset of positive integers, let $k_\lambda$ be the sum of its elements, and let $|\lambda|$ be its number of elements. For a graph $G$, define $h(\lambda)$ to be the maximum integer $t$ such that every $K_t$-minor-free graph is $\lambda$-choosable. **Refined list Hadwiger's conjecture.** There are functions $\phi,\psi:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\psi(n)=\infty
$$

and, for any multiset $\lambda$ of positive integers, if $k_\lambda\geqslant\phi(k_\lambda-|\lambda|)$, then

$$
k_\lambda-h(\lambda)\geqslant\psi(k_\lambda-|\lambda|).
$$

The quantity $k_\lambda-|\lambda|$ measures the distance between $\lambda$-choosability and ordinary $k_\lambda$-colourability. The conjecture asserts that, once $k_\lambda$ is sufficiently large relative to this distance, the gap between $k_\lambda$ and $h(\lambda)$ must grow without bound. The paper proves this for several families of multisets, but whether it holds for all $\lambda$ remains open.

technical_assessment: Lambda-choosability is not defined. A bounded defect family or ordinary list-coloring obstruction does not give growing gap for all large defects with the stated threshold quantifiers.

title: The kernel-growth conjecture for optimal OGF coefficients
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $\mathcal{D}(n,k)$ be a fixed lower-triangular invertible kernel, and define

$$
M_{\mathcal{D},k}(x):=\sum_{n\leq x}\mathcal{D}^{-1}(n,k),\qquad 1\leq k\leq x.

Suppose that

$$
\delta^{1/2}=\inf\left\{\rho>0:\max_{1\leq k\leq x}M_{\mathcal{D},k}(x)=O\left(x^{\rho+\varepsilon}\right),\ \forall\varepsilon>0\right\}.
$$

**Kernel-growth conjecture.** An optimal ordinary generating function $\mathcal{C}(q)$ with integer-valued coefficients, $\mathcal{C}(0)\neq 0$, that attains the theoretical maximum of $\operatorname{Corr}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})$ satisfies

$$
\rho_{\mathcal{C}}(n)\asymp n^{\delta}\qquad(n\to\infty).
$$

Thus $\rho_{\mathcal{C}}(n)$ is bounded above and below in absolute value by constant multiples of $n^{\delta}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. The conjecture connects growth of optimal generating-function coefficients with summatory growth of the inverse kernel; no resolution is supplied.

title: Sun's general conjecture on linear and circular restricted sumsets
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $G$ be an additive group with $|G|>1$. For finite subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ of $G$, define

$$
L(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=\{a_1+\cdots+a_n:a_i\in A_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n,\text{ and }a_i\ne a_{i+1}\text{ for }0<i<n\}
$$

and

$$
C(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=\{a_1+\cdots+a_n:a_i\in A_i\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n,\ a_i\ne a_{i+1}\text{ for }0<i<n,\text{ and }a_n\ne a_1\}.
$$

Let $n>1$ and assume that $|A_i|>1$ for every $i=1,\ldots,n$. The **Sun restricted-sumset conjecture.**

$$
|L(A_1,\ldots,A_n)|\geqslant\min\left\{p(G),\,|A_1|+\cdots+|A_n|-2n+1+\{n\}_2\right\}
$$

and

$$
|C(A_1,\ldots,A_n)|\geqslant\min\left\{p(G),\,|A_1|+\cdots+|A_n|-2n+(-1)^n(1+\{n\}_2)\right\},
$$

where $p(G)$ is the minimum of the orders of the nonzero elements of $G$, interpreted as $+\infty$ if every nonzero element has infinite order, and $\{n\}_2$ denotes the least nonnegative residue of $n$ modulo $2$. This conjecture proposes general lower bounds for the two restricted sumsets introduced by Sun; the source does not state a resolution, so its status remains open.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every additive group, n>1 and finite Ai of sizes >1 satisfy both stated lower bounds in terms of p(G) and parity.
technical_assessment: Polynomial-method arguments over fields do not automatically cover arbitrary additive groups and unequal sets. Cyclic examples are parameter cases; no general compression or group reduction proved.

title: Equality of hypergraph and graph zero-free loci
statement_exact_utf8:
For a positive integer $\Delta$, let $\mathcal U_\Delta$ be the maximal simply connected open subset of $\mathbb C$ containing $0$ that is zero-free for the independence polynomials of all graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$. Thus $\mathcal U_\Delta=\mathcal U_{\Delta,2}$.

**Zero-free locus conjecture.** The zero-free locus of hypergraphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ is identical to the zero-free locus of graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$:

$$
\mathcal U_{\Delta,\geq 2}=\mathcal U_\Delta.
$$

This asks whether allowing arbitrary edge sizes gives no smaller zero-free locus than graphs. The paper notes that its general zero-free disk theorem gives a disk of radius $\lambda_s(\Delta+1)$ inside $\mathcal U_{\Delta,\geq 2}$, but the equality of the full loci remains open.

title: Glock, Kühn and Osthus's Euler-tour threshold conjecture
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $k$ be an integer with $k\geq 3$. An **Euler tour** in a $k$-graph is a cyclic sequence of vertices in which every $k$ cyclically consecutive vertices form an edge and every edge appears uniquely. The **Euler-tour threshold** $\delta^{(k)}_{\mathrm{Euler}}$ is the least $d>0$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, all sufficiently large $k$-graphs with minimum codegree at least $(d+\varepsilon)n$ and every vertex degree divisible by $k$ admit an Euler tour. **Glock, Kühn and Osthus's conjecture.**

$$
\delta^{(k)}_{\mathrm{Euler}}\leq\frac{k-1}{k}.
$$

The source records that an earlier conjecture asserting $\delta^{(k)}_{\mathrm{Euler}}=1/2$ for all $k\geq3$ was disproved, since $\delta^{(3)}_{\mathrm{Euler}}=2/3$. Thus the earlier $1/2$ conjecture is refuted, while the displayed upper-bound conjecture is presented as the subsequent conjecture.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every k>=3 has asymptotic divisible-degree Euler-tour threshold <=(k-1)/k.
technical_assessment: Counterexample to earlier threshold 1/2 for k=3 is compatible with displayed 2/3 bound. No present upper-bound refutation follows; arbitrary-k tour decomposition is substantial.

title: Uniform-edge conjecture for the expected maximum matching in random bipartite graphs
statement_exact_utf8: Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $n$ vertices on each side. A **fractional bipartite matching** is a collection of edge probabilities $x=(x_{uv})$ satisfying the vertex constraints $\sum_v x_{uv}=1$ and $\sum_u x_{uv}=1$. Let $R(x)$ be the random bipartite graph in which each edge $(u,v)$ appears independently with probability $x_{uv}$. Equivalently, let $A=(a_{ij})$ be a doubly stochastic $n\times n$ matrix, with $x_{uv}=a_{ij}$ for corresponding vertices. **Uniform-edge conjecture.** The expected size of the maximum matching in $R(x)$ is minimized when $x_{uv}=1/n$ for every edge. Equivalently, for a random bipartite graph whose edge $(i,j)$ appears independently with probability $a_{ij}$, the expected maximum matching size is minimized when $a_{ij}=1/n$ for all $(i,j)$. The uniform instance is known to have expected maximum matching size $(\gamma+o(1))n$, where $\gamma=2(1-\lambda)-\lambda^2$ and $\lambda=e^{-\lambda}$; the conjecture asserts that this instance is worst among all fractional matchings in $K_{n,n}$.

title: Strength–super edge-magic deficiency conjecture for trees
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $T$ be a nontrivial tree. A **numbering** of $T$ is a bijection $f:V(T)\to\{1,2,\ldots,|V(T)|\}$, and its strength is

$$
\operatorname{str}_f(T)=\max\{f(u)+f(v):uv\in E(T)\}.
$$

The strength of $T$ is

$$
\operatorname{str}(T)=\min_f\operatorname{str}_f(T),
$$

where the minimum is over all numberings, and $\mu_s(T)$ denotes the super edge-magic deficiency of $T$. **Strength–super edge-magic deficiency conjecture.** For every nontrivial tree $T$, there exists some positive constant $c$ such that

$$
\operatorname{str}(T)\geq c\cdot\mu_s(T)+|V(T)|+1.
$$

The paper notes that the known equality $\operatorname{str}(T)=|V(T)|+1$ for every nontrivial tree would make this conjecture imply the conjecture that every nontrivial tree is super edge-magic. Its status is not resolved in the source.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every nontrivial tree T admits c>0 with strength >=c*mu_s(T)+|V|+1.
technical_assessment: Super edge-magic deficiency is undefined in the record. Given stated strength equality, any positive c forces zero deficiency, so weakening c by dependence on T does not give a new easy inequality.

title: The weighted clique-packing conjecture for uniform weights on a clique independent set
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $m\geq 1$ and $k\geq 2$, and let $w$ be an $m$-weighting of $G$. A **$k$-clique independent set** is a set $I$ of vertices such that every $k$-clique of $G$ contains exactly one vertex of $I$. An $m$-weighting $w'$ is **uniform on $I$** when the weights assigned by $w'$ to the vertices of $I$ are equal. **Weighted clique-packing conjecture.** There exist a $k$-clique independent set $I$ of $G$ and an $m$-weighting $w'$ of $G$ uniform on $I$ such that

$$
\pi_k(G(w'))\leq\pi_k(G(w)).
$$

for every $m$-weighting $w$ of $G$. The preceding theorems establish the analogous minimization statement for several graph classes, while the theorem for $k=3$ shows that uniformity on all vertices need not attain the minimum; the conjecture proposes that uniformity on a suitable $k$-clique independent set always suffices.

technical_assessment: m-weighting, G(w), pi_k and allowed graph class omitted; K_(k+1) need not even possess a set meeting every k-clique exactly once. Such literal domain failure is not a new weighted-packing result.

title: The maximality conjecture for Gaussian Riemann derivatives
statement_exact_utf8:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $D_{\mathcal{A}}$ be an $n$-th generalized Riemann differentiation without excess. A generalized Riemann differentiation is called **Gaussian** when it is one of the Gaussian Riemann derivatives introduced in the paper, and **symmetric Gaussian** when it is the corresponding symmetric derivative. For a function $f$ and point $x$, write $f_{(k)}(x)$ and $f_{(k)}^s(x)$ for the $k$-th Peano and symmetric Peano derivatives, respectively.

**Maximality conjecture for Gaussian Riemann derivatives.** For all functions $f$ and points $x$:

1. If $D_{\mathcal{A}}$ is not Gaussian, then

$$
\text{both }f_{(n-1)}(x)\text{ and }D_{\mathcal{A}}f(x)\text{ exist}\ \Longrightarrow\ f_{(n)}(x)\text{ exists}
$$

should be false.

2. If $n\geq 3$ and $D_{\mathcal{A}}$ is symmetric but not symmetric Gaussian, then

$$
\text{both }f_{(n-2)}^s(x)\text{ and }D_{\mathcal{A}}f(x)\text{ exist}\ \Longrightarrow\ f_{(n)}^s(x)\text{ exists}
$$

should be false.

The conjecture identifies the Gaussian and symmetric Gaussian derivatives as the largest classes for which the generalized Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund equivalences can hold. Part (i) is known for $n=1,2$ and remains open for $n\geq 3$; part (ii) is false for $n=1,2$, true for $n=3,4$, and remains open for $n\geq 5$.
quantifiers_reviewed: Every non-Gaussian differentiation without excess must fail the relevant Peano implication; symmetric clause for n>=3 separately.
technical_assessment: Gaussian node families and differentiation normalization omitted, quantifier over witness f is garbled, and small-n status contradicts quoted source. Cannot promote a small-n example without restoring exact Conjecture B.
